solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tablet providing IT support? (6)

blocks.note: the surface wants a tablet computer; the setter means a pill
the surface wants a tech helpdesk; IT is the old euphemism for sex, and the support is physical

annotation.surface: A pill that sorts out your computer problems, like a helpdesk in tablet form.
annotation.walkthrough: IT reads as information technology, but here it is the old euphemism for sex, and the support is of a more physical kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Viagra is the tablet taken to help a man sustain an erection.

entries.clue: Holiday trade making second arrival at front (8)

indicators.note: the new letter is made the second letter of the word
it goes in near the front, replacing what was there

blocks.note: a vocation is a calling or trade
A = arrival, as on timetables; it replaces the O in second place

annotation.surface: A travel-industry remark about holiday bookings and who gets to the resort first.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one letter changes: the O of VOCATION gives way to A, the timetable abbreviation for arrival.
annotation.definitionFit: A vacation is a holiday, especially in American usage.

entries.clue: Gas main centrally located by river (3)

indicators.note: only the letters located at the centre of the word are taken
the next piece is placed beside it

blocks.note: the two central letters of mAIn

annotation.surface: A utility notice: the gas main runs beside the river.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes "Gas main" a single piece of pipework; split it, and Gas is the definition while main is raw material.
annotation.definitionFit: Air is a mixture of gases, loosely called a gas.

entries.clue: Show on NOW (9)

annotation.surface: A television listing: the show airing on NOW, the channel.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make NOW look like a broadcaster's name; it simply means the present time.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a painting that shows a battle represents it.

entries.clue: A turn in Cream or Foreigner (8)

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are turned about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of IN CREAM rearranged

annotation.surface: A music-hall act set among the classic rock bands Cream and Foreigner.
annotation.walkthrough: Cream and Foreigner are both rock bands, and turn suggests a stage act; in fact turn rearranges IN CREAM, and Foreigner is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: to a British setter and solver, anyone from the United States is from abroad.

entries.clue: Jesus mostly drinks no port (7)

indicators.note: most of the word, dropping its last letter
takes the next piece inside, as a drinker takes in a drink

annotation.surface: A remark about Jesus declining a glass of port, and drinking only a little.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes port a drink; here it is a harbour town, Messina in Sicily.
annotation.definitionFit: Messina is a port city in Sicily on the strait of the same name.

entries.clue: Dish cook left by a slice of iceberg (5)

indicators.note: the A departs from the word before it
only the first letter of the following word is taken

annotation.surface: A kitchen instruction: plate the dish beside a wedge of iceberg lettuce.
annotation.walkthrough: The a belongs to the deletion, not to the slice: A leaves ROAST, and the slice is just the I of iceberg.
annotation.definitionFit: Rosti is a Swiss dish of fried grated potato.

entries.clue: Net contains supply for North African city (11)

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple: bending the letters about

annotation.surface: A trade note: a net contains the stock shipped to a North African city.
annotation.walkthrough: Supply looks like a noun; read it as supple-ly, flexibly, and it tells you to bend the letters of NET CONTAINS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Algeria's third-largest city, in the north-east of the country, named after the Roman emperor.

entries.clue: Fat chance of fellow being stuck up on rocks (2,4)

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read bottom to top
in a down clue, placed on top of the next piece

blocks.note: a don is a fellow of a college
on the rocks = served over ice

annotation.surface: A college fellow, snooty and stranded on rocks, has little hope of rescue.
annotation.walkthrough: Stuck up looks like an insult to the fellow; in a down clue it reverses DON, and rocks is bar slang for ice cubes.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways to say there is no hope of something happening.

entries.clue: A sweet given to diner ultimately is sharper (6)

indicators.note: the pieces are joined together
only the last letter of the word is taken

annotation.surface: A restaurant-goer is handed a dessert and becomes more alert.
annotation.walkthrough: Sweet looks like a pudding for the diner; it is the adjective cute.
annotation.definitionFit: Acute means sharp, so acuter means sharper.

entries.clue: Fish experts holding key for cases (9)

indicators.note: the outer piece holds the key inside it

blocks.note: A is a musical key; it goes between CAR and P

annotation.surface: Specialist anglers keep a key for their tackle cases.
annotation.walkthrough: Key is a musical key, A, sitting inside CARP rather than anything that opens a case.
annotation.definitionFit: Carapaces are the hard upper shells or cases of crabs, tortoises and the like.

entries.clue: Some in catalepsy nodding in assembly (5)

indicators.note: only some letters from within the following words are taken

annotation.surface: Some members of a gathering are dozing off, one of them almost in a trance.
annotation.walkthrough: Catalepsy is a trance-like rigid state, which suits the picture of nodding off in a meeting.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind: the word names a formal church council of clergy and delegates.

entries.clue: Flood in Split on other side of hill (7)

indicators.note: the first piece comes after the second

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

annotation.surface: A flood reported in Split, the Croatian city, over the far side of a hill.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital makes Split the Croatian city, but it is the verb, past tense of rend.
annotation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing flood of water.

entries.clue: Brit involved with routine punishment (11)

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up with each other

annotation.surface: A British person caught up in a regular regime of punishment.
annotation.walkthrough: Brit and routine sit side by side and share all eleven letters; the surface makes involved read as mixed up in something, which is exactly the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Retribution is punishment inflicted in return for a wrong.

entries.clue: I fleece and jerk around one stupid (7)

indicators.note: joins the pieces in order
the first word goes around the next piece

blocks.note: to do someone is to swindle or fleece them
I = one, the Roman numeral; it goes inside DO
a tic is an involuntary jerk

annotation.surface: A confession: I cheat people and flail about, like a fool.
annotation.walkthrough: Around applies to the fleece piece only; the jerk piece follows untouched. The surface reads I as a speaker confessing, but it is just a letter here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an idiotic remark is a stupid one.

entries.clue: Lean hero in debt sadly thus? (2,3,9)

definitions.text: Lean hero in debt sadly thus?

indicators.note: the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

annotation.surface: A thin, indebted protagonist, a hard-up hero down on his luck.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: a lean hero in debt is exactly someone on the breadline, and the same words rearranged spell it.
annotation.definitionFit: On the breadline means living in poverty, which fits a lean, indebted hero.

entries.clue: Sweets in lounge I put by old man (9)

indicators.note: the pieces are placed next to each other

annotation.surface: Sweets tucked away in the sitting room, left by Dad's chair.
annotation.walkthrough: Lounge looks like a room; it is the verb loll.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind: hard sweets on a stick, so the plural matches the plural Sweets.

entries.clue: In a tizzy, I get data mixed up (8)

indicators.note: things that are mixed up are out of their proper order, so the letters before it must be put into a new one

annotation.surface: Someone flustered keeps muddling their figures.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and the comma is only a pause; the surface is apt, since muddled data is what makes people flustered.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a tizzy is a state of nervous excitement, so being in one is being flustered and on edge.

entries.clue: Protected structure in Pisan tower? (6,8)

blocks.note: a building given legal protection for its historic value
to list is to lean; the Leaning Tower of Pisa is a building that has listed

annotation.surface: A heritage note about a protected monument in Pisa.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a listed building is one on the official register of protected historic buildings; the question mark flags the second reading, listed as in tilted.
annotation.definitionFit: A listed building is a structure protected by law; Pisa's tower has literally listed.

entries.clue: Sailor overlooked by Times or Sun (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits below the second

blocks.note: days = times, as in 'in my days'

annotation.surface: A sailor ignored by both The Times and The Sun, two British newspapers.
annotation.walkthrough: Times and Sun read as rival newspapers; Times gives DAYS and Sun is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A poetic use: the star that brings the day, a literary name for our sun.

entries.clue: One sending one down free of restraints? (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the letter I (one) is moved further down the word

annotation.surface: A prisoner who sends another person to jail, then walks free, unshackled.
annotation.walkthrough: Sending down sounds like jailing someone; here one is the letter I, and it drops one place in UNITED.
annotation.definitionFit: Untied means freed from ties or restraints.

entries.clue: The King in bed is right laugh (6)

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: a seam is a bed or layer of coal or rock
CR = Carolus Rex, King Charles; it goes inside SEAM

annotation.surface: Finding the monarch in your bed would be hilarious.
annotation.walkthrough: Bed is a geological layer, not furniture. A right laugh is British slang for something very funny.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: British informal speech calls a very funny person or event both a scream and a right laugh.

entries.clue: Noble’s extremely ropey in a state (7)

indicators.note: only the extremes, first and last letters, of the word are taken

annotation.surface: An aristocrat who is looking the worse for wear, shabby and in a bad state.
annotation.walkthrough: In a state sounds like distress; ropey is British slang for poor or unwell. Here state is a nation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sovereign state such as France is a nation with its own government and borders.

entries.clue: Demonstrations abandoned by expert pilots? (5)

indicators.note: the named piece leaves the word

blocks.note: a pro is an expert; it is removed

annotation.surface: Protest marches that seasoned aircraft pilots have given up on.
annotation.walkthrough: Pilots reads as flyers, but a pilot is also a trial run, so pilots are tests; the question mark marks that twist.
annotation.definitionFit: A pilot is a test or trial version, so pilots are tests.

entries.clue: Piece of shrapnel off thunderous weapon (7)

indicators.note: take only a piece, the first letter, of the word
that letter is taken off the following word

blocks.note: strident = loud, thunderous; the S comes off

annotation.surface: A war report: a fragment of shrapnel flies off a deafening weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a war report, but the definition is weapon; the S of shrapnel comes off STRIDENT.
annotation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, a weapon.

entries.clue: Does one survive, having turned tail? (5)

indicators.note: the tail end of the word is turned round

blocks.note: to exist is to survive; its last two letters swap

annotation.surface: A question about whether anyone lives through it after running away.
annotation.walkthrough: Does one reads as a question opener; it is British slang, to do one meaning to clear off.
annotation.definitionFit: To do one is British slang for to leave, so does one = exits.

entries.clue: Channel broadcasting telethons (3,6)

indicators.note: the letters are scattered about, as seed is broadcast

annotation.surface: A TV channel showing fundraising telethons.
annotation.walkthrough: Channel is a waterway, not a TV station: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland.
annotation.definitionFit: The Solent is a sea channel off the south coast of England.

entries.clue: Lamp this writer picked up (3)

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, heard

annotation.surface: A writer picks up a lamp from the desk.
annotation.walkthrough: Lamps is old slang for eyes, so one lamp is an eye.
annotation.definitionFit: Old slang: the eyes were called lamps because they are what lets you see.

entries.clue: Government department tax on small motors (8)

indicators.note: the first piece is placed after the second

blocks.note: to tax someone's patience is to try it

annotation.surface: A government department imposes a levy on small cars.
annotation.walkthrough: Tax looks like a levy, which suits the department; it is the verb try, as in trying patience.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Ministry of Defence is the department of state run by a minister.

entries.clue: A conservative in post gets rise (6)

indicators.note: the piece goes inside the next word

blocks.note: C = Conservative; it goes inside SEND

annotation.surface: A Tory in a job wins a pay rise.
annotation.walkthrough: Post looks like a job; it is the verb send.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a balloon that goes up can be said to rise or to ascend.
